title: JANUS Engine R2D — dual-battery support and regeneration architecture
idea: Use two independently managed batteries so one can support Axle rotation/startup/transients while the other is preferentially available to receive genuine regenerative or process surplus, then alternate roles under a supervisory controller.

key_physics.support_not_primary_drive: A support battery may provide only the torque deficit required to hold target RPM. If hydraulic/process torque carries most of the load, battery power can be small and eventually fall to zero.
key_physics.two_batteries_do_not_create_energy: Alternating Battery A and Battery B does not change total energy conservation. Charge moved from one battery through motor/generator paths is reduced by conversion losses unless an independent source adds energy.
key_physics.valid_regen: Battery charge is genuine recovered energy only when traced to independently measured hydraulic/mechanical work, PEMFC electrical surplus, or rotor kinetic-energy reduction.
key_physics.benefit_of_two_buffers: Two packs can improve isolation, startup availability, pulse handling, regenerative headroom, redundancy and measurement clarity even though they do not improve the thermodynamic ceiling.

BAT_A_SUPPORT: minimum reserve SOC protected from opportunistic charging loads
BAT_B_RECOVERY: preferred sink for verified PEMFC/process surplus
maintain charging headroom so regeneration is not clipped by a full support pack
proposed_roles.ROLE_SWAP: When SOC, temperature, health and reserve rules permit, A and B may swap roles so cycle wear is balanced and either pack can become the startup reserve.

power_path: BAT_A/B <-> bidirectional DC/DC stages <-> common DC bus <-> coreless AFPM + auxiliaries + PEMFC
why_not_direct_battery_swapping: Direct alternation without bidirectional power electronics can create uncontrolled equalization currents and poor SOC control. The architecture should use isolated or appropriately controlled bidirectional conversion/contactors and BMS supervision.

energy_ledger.proof_metric: With external charger disconnected, compare E_A + E_B at start and end of the stabilized test, not either battery alone.
energy_ledger.battery_neutral_rule: E_A_end + E_B_end >= E_A_start + E_B_start over the declared stabilized hold before any claim of battery-neutral self-drive.
energy_ledger.export_rule: Only energy above internal loads plus restoration of both declared reserve SOC targets is exportable surplus.

important_advantage.regen_headroom: Keeping one pack below full SOC gives the generator somewhere to put short regenerative pulses even when the support pack must remain near its startup reserve target.
important_advantage.measurement_clarity: Separating support and recovery paths makes it easier to distinguish consumed startup/support Wh from genuinely recovered Wh.
important_advantage.reliability: Either pack can preserve controlled shutdown or restart capability if the other is isolated by the BMS.

test_matrix: hydraulic torque sweep through motor-current zero into regeneration
pass_condition: Dual-battery architecture is retained if it reduces startup/support stress, preserves regeneration headroom or improves reliability/measurement while total E_A+E_B accounting remains closed and added DC/DC/BMS losses are acceptable.
